notes.h: How to read the merit column
p: Green — strong / likely automatic merit at 3.8 / 1170
Yellow — possible, not assured (waiver or test-optional path)
Light red — unlikely or $0 automatic at 1170
Ole Miss, Texas Tech and ASU are the merit-friendly fits at 1170; UGA, UT Austin and Auburn are reaches on scores; SMU is the cost outlier (private). AP ranks move weekly — see Sources & notes.

notes.h: How to read the need-based aid column
p: Federal baseline (2026-27 FAFSA): SAI floor −$1,500; maximum Pell Grant $7,395. Family-owned businesses with ≤100 employees are EXCLUDED from FAFSA assets (One Big Beautiful Bill Act); max-Pell filers skip asset questions entirely. With the family's −$203K AGI, max Pell is likely and SAI should sit near the floor.

NONE of the 11 meets full demonstrated need for out-of-state students, and EVERY signature free-tuition program is resident-only — realistic OOS package is max Pell ($7,395) + modest institutional aid, leaving a gap at OOS rates.

notes.h: How to read the residency column
p: In all 7 states, a dependent under-24 freshman with out-of-state parents has no realistic path to in-state tuition after year one; parents relocating to the state is the clean route.

notes.h: How to read the test policy column
p: Test-required = every applicant must submit SAT or ACT scores; no test-optional path. Test-optional = the student chooses whether to submit; no penalty for not submitting for ADMISSION — but scores can still be required for automatic merit scholarships (Alabama: test-optional forfeits the automatic merit grid; Ole Miss: the $9,000/yr grid needs the score submitted; Auburn: scores gate scholarships; Texas Tech: submitting the 1170 raises the automatic award from $3,000 to $4,000/yr).

Shep-specific read: at test-optional schools where his 1170 sits below the 25th percentile (SMU, UGA n/a since required), do NOT submit for admission — but DO submit where it unlocks automatic merit (Ole Miss, Texas Tech, Alabama if he retakes to 1200+).

src: Undergrad enrollment

Undergraduate enrollment only (degree-seeking undergraduates where CDS distinguishes; otherwise total undergraduate headcount), Fall 2024 IPEDS / Common Data Set B1 / university IR — NOT total headcount with graduate/professional students. Figures verified Oct 5, 2026: UGA 32,399 (IPEDS Fall Enrollment), FSU 32,720 (IPEDS 2024-25; FSU Fact Book Fall 2024 reports 32,356 degree-seeking + unclassified split), ASU 65,450 — Arizona State University Campus Immersion (Tempe) undergraduates only; ASU's system-wide total across all campuses + ASU Online is far larger (~159k+ total, ~120k undergrad system-wide) and is NOT used here, Tennessee (UTK) 30,564, UT Austin 43,165, Texas Tech 32,580 (IPEDS; TTU IR Trends reports 32,792), Texas A&M (College Station) 60,710 (IPEDS; TAMU reports 57,659 College Station campus undergraduates excluding Galveston/McAllen system counts), SMU 7,285, Alabama 34,389, Ole Miss 21,585, Auburn 27,907 (CDS B1 Total Undergraduates; degree-seeking 26,816). Sources: IPEDS Data Center / College Navigator Fall 2024, university Common Data Sets 2024-25, and university IR fact books.
Acceptance rate
Most recent freshman admit rate published (Class of 2029 / Fall 2025 cycle where available; otherwise IPEDS 2024). UGA 33% reflects the Class of 2029 overall rate.
Avg GPA / SAT

Admitted-student mid-50% ranges unless labeled 'avg'. UGA GPA is UGA-recalculated core GPA. UT Austin does not publish an official GPA/SAT profile — figures shown are outside estimates and are flagged as such.
Tuition & fees / yr
Published tuition & fees only (excludes room, board, books). In-state / out-of-state shown for publics; SMU is private (single rate). Confirm on each school's net-price calculator before budgeting.
Merit at 3.8 / 1170

Judged against each school's published automatic-merit grid/waiver rules as of Oct 2026. Green = automatic/likely on the grid; Yellow = possible via waiver or test-optional review, not assured; Light red = below published floors / no automatic merit. Retaking the SAT to 1200 (Alabama) or 1300 (Tennessee) changes the answer at those schools.
Football AP rank

AP Top 25, Week 6, released Oct 4, 2026 (via NCAA.com): #1 Texas, #2 Georgia, #6 Alabama, #9 Ole Miss, #11 Texas Tech, #15 Tennessee, #24 SMU. FSU, ASU, Texas A&M and Auburn were unranked with no votes in that poll. Ranks change weekly.
% Greek
Share of undergraduates in fraternities/sororities, most recent campus-life / Common Data Set reporting. Ole Miss shown as ~35–39% range across sources; UGA ~25%.
IM + club sports
Club-sport team counts and intramural offerings from each university's recreation/club-sports pages, accessed Oct 2026. Counts vary by semester as clubs form/dissolve.
Flagged uncertainties

• UT Austin GPA/SAT: outside estimates only — UT publishes neither.
• Alabama out-of-state tuition varies by source (~$34.7k–$36.7k); ~$34,660 used.
• Auburn SAT band: a conflicting third-party figure exists; 1260–1390 is the university-published mid-50%.
• ASU club-sport count unverified (intramural 12+ verified).
• Tennessee intramural count unpublished (47 club teams verified).
Residency note
Merit and tuition assume out-of-state (non-resident) status unless a school's in-state rate is what Shep would pay. Residency changes both tuition and merit eligibility — confirm per school.
Need-based aid outlook

2026-27 FAFSA — SAI floor −$1,500 (FSA Handbook 2026-27 Vol 1 Ch 1); maximum Pell Grant $7,395 (ED Dear Colleague Letter Jan 30 2026). Family-owned businesses with ≤100 employees are EXCLUDED from FAFSA assets under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Pub. L. 119-21); max-Pell filers skip asset questions entirely. With the family's −$203K AGI, max Pell is likely and SAI should sit near the floor.
Per-school % of freshman need met and average need grants: from CollegeData / BigFuture / Common Data Set figures as listed — UGA ~78% (CDS 2020-21 — old, flagged), FSU ~75% / ~$15,300, ASU ~59% (non-resident Pell freshmen only ~38%), Tennessee ~59% / ~$15,900, UT Austin ~71% / ~$20,800, Texas Tech ~59% / ~$12,400, Texas A&M ~70% / ~$13,200, SMU ~88.6% / ~$48,400, Alabama ~64.6% / ~$19,100, Ole Miss % of need met unverified (flagged), Auburn ~60% / ~$12,000. Signature free-tuition programs (Obama Scholars, UT Promise, Texas Advance Commitment, Red Raider Guarantee, Aggie Assurance, Ole Miss Opportunity) are resident-only in every case. NONE of the 11 meets full demonstrated need for out-of-state students; realistic OOS package is max Pell ($7,395) + modest institutional aid, leaving a gap at OOS rates.
In-state tuition after yr 1?

Dependent-student residency rules make reclassification effectively unavailable for a dependent under-24 freshman with out-of-state parents in all 7 states:
• Texas — dependent domicile follows the parent (Texas Educ. Code §54.052); students who move to TX for school are presumed non-residents. UT Austin: no realistic dependent path. Texas Tech and Texas A&M: same rule, but a non-resident competitive scholarship of ≥$1,000 (Tech) or ≥$4,000/yr (A&M) triggers the in-state tuition waiver.
• Arizona — ABOR residency policy presumes against full-time students; requires proven financial independence (Arizona State).
• Georgia — USG Board of Regents: cannot gain in-state status while attending without clear evidence of domicile for non-educational purposes (UGA).
• Florida — F.S. §1009.21: dependent students need a parent with 12 months FL legal residence (Florida State).
• Tennessee — TBR rule: un-emancipated student's domicile is the parent's (University of Tennessee).
• Alabama — Auburn / Alabama residency pages: moving to AL primarily for college doesn't establish intent; extremely difficult under 24 with non-AL parents (Alabama, Auburn).
• Mississippi — Ole Miss catalog (legal residence): strictest of the group; independent residency only after age 21 + 12 months + proven financial independence.
SMU is private with a single tuition rate. In all states, parents relocating to the state is the clean route to in-state tuition.
Test policy

Verified Oct 5, 2026 for the 2026-27 admissions cycle. Test-required = every applicant must submit SAT or ACT scores; no test-optional path. Test-optional = the student chooses whether to submit; no penalty for not submitting for ADMISSION — but scores can still be required for automatic merit scholarships (Alabama: test-optional forfeits the automatic merit grid; Ole Miss: the $9,000/yr grid needs the score submitted; Auburn: scores gate scholarships; Texas Tech: submitting the 1170 raises the automatic award from $3,000 to $4,000/yr).
Per-school: UGA — test-required; FSU — test-required (admissions.fsu.edu; Empowerly); ASU — test-optional; Tennessee — test-required (admissions.utk.edu test-score-policy, Fall 2027); UT Austin — test-required; Texas Tech — test-optional; Texas A&M — test-optional; SMU — test-optional; Alabama — test-optional; Ole Miss — test-optional 2026-27 (olemiss.edu admissions; collegesimply citing IPEDS 2025); Auburn — test-optional.
Shep-specific read: at test-optional schools where his 1170 sits below the 25th percentile (SMU; UGA n/a since required), do NOT submit for admission — but DO submit where it unlocks automatic merit (Ole Miss, Texas Tech, Alabama if he retakes to 1200+).
